neural responses in the human parietal cortex that are believed to be tuned to stimulus numerosity are more accurately predicted by numerosity than by non‐numerical stimulus features, even when these features are known to influence numerosity perception.
neural responses in cognitive areas of the brain need not reflect low-level stimulus properties.
neural responses to numerosity are better explained by numerosity than by other stimulus features, even though numerosity is often correlated with other stimulus features.

the question of how the brain represents the number of items in the world.
the neural basis of numerosity perception and how it is represented in the brain.
the question: what is it that makes a set of objects look more or less numerous to us?

the results of the current study do not provide any evidence that neural numerosity responses can be explained by non-numerical features, but they do not provide any conclusive evidence that they cannot be explained by non-numeric features either.
the numerosity map in human parietal cortex is not simply driven by low-level visual features, but that numerosity is a significant contributor to the neural response.
